requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation on any port from a port array SHALL NOT be used to catch a call timeout.
requirements.original: The catch on any port from a port array operation cannot be used to catch a call timeout.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: The `catch` operation SHALL only be used at procedure-based ports.
requirements.original: a) The catch operation shall only be used at procedure-based ports.

requirements.subject: ent:exception
requirements.canonical: The type of an exception caught by a `catch` operation SHALL be specified in the signature of the procedure that raised the exception.
requirements.original: The type of the caught exception shall be specified in the signature of the procedure that raised the exception.

requirements.subject: ent:port-type
requirements.canonical: The type definition of the port used in a `catch` operation SHALL include in its `out` or `inout` list the signature to which the caught exception belongs.
requirements.original: b) The type definition of the port shall include in its out or inout list the name of the procedure to which the exception belongs.

ambiguity.issue: Port type lists contain signature references; 'procedure' is used loosely for the signature.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation SHALL NOT bind incoming values to the terms of the expression or to the template.
requirements.original: c) No binding of the incoming values to the terms of the expression or to the template shall occur.

requirements.subject: ent:redirection-part
requirements.canonical: The assignment of exception values to variables SHALL be made in the redirection (assignment) part of the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: The assignment of the exception values to variables shall be made in the assignment part of the catch operation.

ambiguity.issue: The syntax and the semantic description call this the redirection part.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-exception
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation for the timeout exception SHALL only be used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation.
requirements.original: d) Catching timeout exceptions shall be restricted to the exception handling part of a call.

improper_terms.used: exception handling part of a call
improper_terms.proper: response and exception handling part of a call operation

ambiguity.issue: Elsewhere the clause uses 'response and exception handling part'.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-exception
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation that handles the timeout exception SHALL NOT contain further matching criteria, including a `from` clause.
requirements.original: No further matching criteria (including a from part) and no assignment part is allowed for a catch operation that handles a timeout exception.

requirements.subject: ent:timeout-exception
requirements.canonical: A `catch` operation that handles the timeout exception SHALL NOT contain a redirection (assignment) part.
requirements.original: No further matching criteria (including a from part) and no assignment part is allowed for a catch operation that handles a timeout exception.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-any-exception
requirements.canonical: A catch any exception operation SHALL NOT contain a `value` clause, i.e. accepted exception values SHALL NOT be assigned to a variable.
requirements.original: e) Exception values accepted by catch any exception shall not be assigned to a variable, i.e. the value clause shall not be present.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-any-exception
requirements.condition: CatchAnyException is used in the response and exception handling part of a call operation
requirements.canonical: If a catch any exception operation is used in the response and exception handling part of a `call` operation, it SHALL only treat exceptions raised by the procedure invoked by that `call` operation.
requirements.original: f) If CatchAnyException is used in the response and exception handling part of a call operation, it shall only treat exceptions raised by the procedure invoked by the call operation.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: Every AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `catch` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: g) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the catch operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.canonical: Every ValueRef in the `sender` clause of a `catch` operation SHALL be of type `address`, of a component type, or of the address type bound to the port type of the port instance referenced in the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: g) All AddressRef items in the from clause and all ValueRef items in the sender clause shall be of type address, component or of the address type bound to the port type (see clause 6.2.9) of the port instance referenced in the catch operation.

requirements.subject: ent:from-clause
requirements.canonical: An AddressRef in the `from` clause of a `catch` operation SHALL NOT contain the special value `null` at the time of the operation.
requirements.original: No AddressRef in the from clause shall contain the special value null at the time of the operation.

requirements.subject: ent:any-from-port-array
requirements.canonical: The PortArrayRef in an `any from` `catch` operation SHALL be a reference to a completely initialized port array.
requirements.original: h) The PortArrayRef shall be a reference to a completely initialized port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.canonical: The index redirection (`@index value`) in a `catch` operation SHALL only be used when the operation is used on an `any from` port array construct.
requirements.original: i) The index redirection shall only be used when the operation is used on an any from port array construct.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for single-dimensional arrays
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a single-dimensional port array, the type of the integer variable SHALL allow storing the highest index of the respective port array.
requirements.original: j) If the index redirection is used for single-dimensional arrays, the type of the integer variable shall allow storing the highest index of the respective port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the size of the integer array or `record of integer` variable SHALL be exactly the same as the dimension of the respective port array.
requirements.original: k) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.

requirements.subject: ent:index-redirection
requirements.condition: the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays
requirements.canonical: If the index redirection is used for a multi-dimensional port array, the element type of the integer array or `record of integer` variable SHALL allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.
requirements.original: k) If the index redirection is used for multi-dimensional arrays, the size of the integer array or record of integer type shall exactly be the same as the dimension of the respective port array, and the its type shall allow storing the highest index (from all dimensions) of the port array.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.condition: the referenced variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: If a variable referenced in the `value`, `sender` or `@index` clause of a `catch` operation is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to that variable IS equal to the result produced by the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: l) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the catch operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the catch operation.

requirements.subject: ent:lazy-variable
requirements.condition: the referenced variable is a lazy or fuzzy variable
requirements.canonical: A later evaluation of a lazy or fuzzy variable assigned in the redirection part of a `catch` operation IS NOT a repeated invocation of the `catch` operation.
requirements.original: l) If a variable referenced in the value, sender or @index clause is a lazy or fuzzy variable, the expression assigned to this variable is equal to the result produced by the catch operation, i.e. later evaluation of the lazy or fuzzy variable does not lead to repeated invocation of the catch operation.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: the catch operation contains both from and sender clause
requirements.canonical: If a `catch` operation contains both a `from` and a `sender` clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause SHALL be type compatible with the template in the `from` clause.
requirements.original: m) If the catch operation contains both from and sender clause, the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause shall be type compatible with the template in the from clause.

requirements.subject: ent:sender-clause
requirements.condition: the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause
requirements.canonical: If a `catch` operation contains a `sender` clause but no `from` clause, the sender SHALL be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: If the operation contains a sender clause but no from clause, the sender shall be type compatible with the variable or parameter referenced in the sender clause.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.canonical: A type mismatch error CAN occur if the types in the receive part are not compatible with the types in the assignment part, or, if the `from` clause is missing, if the type of the sender can be determined and is not type compatible with the type in the `sender` clause.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: An error due to a type mismatch may happen if the types in the receive part are not compatible to the types in the assignment part or, if the from clause is missing, but the type of the sender can be determined and it is not type compatible with the type in the sender clause.

improper_terms.proper: matching part (signature and template instance) of the catch operation

ambiguity.issue: The note is copied from the receive operation; for catch the 'receive part' is the exception matching part.

requirements.subject: ent:decoded-modifier
requirements.condition: the @decoded modifier is used and the matched field uses decmatch
requirements.canonical: When an exception field is assigned with the `@decoded` modifier and the value or template to be matched uses MatchDecodedContent (`decmatch`) matching for that field, the type of the template in the `decmatch` matching SHALL be type compatible with the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.
requirements.original: n) When assigning implicitly decoded exception fields (by using the @decoded modifier) in cases where the value or template to be matched uses the MatchDecodedContent (decmatch) matching for the parameter to be stored, the type of the template in the MatchDecodedContent matching shall be type-compatible to the type of the variable the decoded field is stored into.

requirements.subject: ent:catch-operation
requirements.canonical: The value referenced by the ObjectReference before the `catch` keyword, or the return type of a function instance used there, SHALL be of a port type.
requirements.original: o) The referenced value associated with Ref or the return type associated with FunctionInstance followed by the catch keyword, shall be of a port type.

ambiguity.issue: The syntactical structure of the catch operation uses ObjectReference; Ref and FunctionInstance do not appear in it.

requirements.subject: ent:value-clause
requirements.condition: no TemplateInstance is provided in the parameter list
requirements.canonical: If no TemplateInstance is provided in the parameter list of a `catch` operation, the redirection part SHALL NOT contain a `value` clause.
requirements.original: p) If no TemplateInstance is provided in the parameter list, then also no value clause shall be present in the redirection part.

requirements.subject: ent:nodefault-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@nodefault` modifier SHALL only be used in stand-alone `catch` statements.
requirements.original: q) The @nodefault modifier is allowed only in stand-alone catch statements.

non_requirement.reason: Introduction to the restrictions list; points to clause 5 and table 16.
